subject: Mathematics
source: Original supplementary learning draft aligned to Class 6 Ganita Prakash Chapter 10 (fegp110.pdf), Reprint 2026–27. Verify any school-specific edition before publication.
goals: Interpret positive, negative and zero values in context.
Place integers on a number line.
Use opposite numbers to describe equal distances in opposite directions from zero.
summary: Numbers below zero are negative numbers. Positive and negative numbers can describe positions or changes relative to a reference point. On a number line, numbers farther to the right are greater, and numbers farther to the left are smaller.

concepts.title: Zero as a reference
concepts.explanation: Zero can represent a reference level, such as sea level, a starting balance or no change. Positive values are above or beyond the reference in one direction; negative values are below or opposite it.
concepts.example: A temperature of −3°C is three degrees below zero.

concepts.title: The number line
concepts.explanation: Numbers increase from left to right. Negative integers lie left of zero; positive integers lie right of zero. Equal spacing represents equal numerical steps.
concepts.example: −4 lies to the left of −1, so −4 is smaller than −1.

concepts.title: Opposite numbers
concepts.explanation: Opposite numbers are the same distance from zero on opposite sides. Their sum is zero. Zero is its own opposite.
concepts.example: The opposite of 6 is −6; both are six units from zero.

concepts.title: Comparing integers
concepts.explanation: On a number line, the integer farther right is greater. Among negative numbers, the one with the smaller absolute distance from zero is greater.
concepts.example: −2 > −7 because −2 is to the right of −7 and is closer to zero.

workedExamples.question: Order −3, 2, −6, 0 from least to greatest.
steps: Place them on a number line.
Negative values come before zero; among negatives, −6 is left of −3.
Positive 2 is to the right of zero.

workedExamples.question: The temperature rises from −4°C to 3°C. By how many degrees did it rise?

practice.question: Which is greater: −1 or −5?
practice.why: −1 is farther to the right on the number line.

practice.question: What is the opposite of −12?
practice.why: Opposites are equally far from zero on opposite sides.

practice.question: Arrange 4, −2, 0, −7 in increasing order.
practice.why: Move from left to right on the number line.

practice.question: What could −₹50 mean in a simple account context?
practice.answer: It could represent a debt or a balance 50 rupees below zero, depending on the chosen reference convention.
practice.why: The context determines what the sign means.
